description:
FILED s473t3 (Opus triage of the 79 CATALOG-only blessed rows), on main
d9a2aac0.  PRE-EXISTING.  Probes: scratch/s473t3/probes/p15b-method-99-103.pl,
p15c-autoload-cache.pl, p15d-autoload-where.pl.

ROW BEHIND IT (baselines/fail-baseline.tsv, 1 row):
  method.t 103 `AUTOLOAD is nul-clean`
  -- perl-tests/method.t:437-439:
       *NulTest::AUTOLOAD = sub { our $AUTOLOAD; return $AUTOLOAD };
       like(NulTest->${ \"nul\0test" }, qr/nul\0test/, "AUTOLOAD is nul-clean");

REPRODUCER (perl 5.40.3 vs ./runpcl), five variants that isolate it:
    { package B1; sub m1 {1}
      *B1::AUTOLOAD = sub { our $AUTOLOAD; return $AUTOLOAD };   # inside pkg
      package main; print "in-pkg  =[", (eval { B1->later } // "undef"), "]\n" }
    { package B2; sub m1 {1}
      package main;
      *B2::AUTOLOAD = sub { our $AUTOLOAD; return $AUTOLOAD };   # from main
      print "in-main =[", (eval { B2->later } // "undef"), "]\n" }
    { package B3; sub m1 {1}
      package main; *B3::AUTOLOAD = \&B1::AUTOLOAD;              # alias
      print "alias   =[", (eval { B3->later } // "undef"), "]\n" }
    { package B4; sub m1 {1} sub AUTOLOAD { our $AUTOLOAD; return $AUTOLOAD }
      package main; print "declared=[", (eval { B4->later } // "undef"), "]\n" }
    { package B5; sub m1 {1}
      package main; *B5::plainmeth = sub { "PM" };               # NOT AUTOLOAD
      print "plainglob=[", (eval { B5->plainmeth } // "undef"), "]\n" }
  perl: in-pkg=[B1::later] in-main=[B2::later] alias=[B3::later]
        declared=[B4::later] plainglob=[PM]
  PCL : in-pkg=[B1::later] in-main=[undef]     alias=[B1::later]
        declared=[B4::later] plainglob=[PM]

SO THE DISCRIMINATOR IS THE SITE, NOT THE NAME: the same glob assignment
works inside `package B1;` and fails from `package main;`, an ALIAS to a
named sub works from main, and a NON-AUTOLOAD glob assignment from main works.
The failing call returns undef SILENTLY -- perl would either call AUTOLOAD or
die "Can't locate object method", so PCL produces a value perl never can.
(The NUL byte in method.t's method name is a red herring: with the AUTOLOAD
installed inside the package, `NulTest->${\"nul\0test"}` returns
`NulTest::nul\0test` correctly in PCL.)

CATALOG NOTE THIS REPLACES: sweep-bug-catalog.md method.t, "the
AUTOLOAD-via-@ISA cluster ... both hard" (row 103 was filed there with no
mechanism).

FAMILY: AUTOLOAD dispatch; sibling #1485.  Also the cross-package glob-install
family: #83 (import-into-caller glob-install invisible cross-file).


=== FIXED (s532c, Opus agent, 2026-11-06) ===
THE MECHANISM: PCL set `$AUTOLOAD` in the package whose AUTOLOAD GLOB the lookup found (%pcl-set-autoload-var with %pcl-find-autoload-in-isa's package); perl sets it in gv.c's varstash = GvSTASH(CvGV(cv)), the package the AUTOLOAD SUB was DEFINED under -- a named sub's own package, an anonymous sub's compile package.  So `*B2::AUTOLOAD = sub { our $AUTOLOAD; ... }` written from main sets $main::AUTOLOAD in perl (the closure's `our` is main's); PCL set $B2::AUTOLOAD and the closure read undef.  The alias spelling read a STALE $B1::AUTOLOAD the same way.  Found from Template-Toolkit t/proc.t rows 5/7 (Template::Plugin::Procedural compiles its proxy's AUTOLOAD as an anon sub in Procedural and assigns it to *{"${proxy}::AUTOLOAD"}): every procedural plugin method answered "".
FIX: `%p-autoload-var-package FN` (the defining name's package from %pcl-sub-names, else %p-sub-stash-of -- an anon sub's p-anon-sub package) chooses the package; %pcl-set-autoload-var takes the AUTOLOAD function as an optional third argument at its three runtime call sites (method dispatch, SUPER::, a plain call of an undefined sub).  cl/pcl-xs.lisp's site keeps the glob package (XS parked).  All five spellings of the reproducer above now print perl's lines.  Guard `Pl/t/autoload-home-01.t` (2 rows, both FAIL on ce665621).  The perl-tests row method.t 103 `AUTOLOAD is nul-clean` is expected to leave baselines/fail-baseline.tsv -- see the s532c sweep.
subject: SILENT WRONG (AUTOLOAD): `*Pkg::AUTOLOAD = sub {...}` written from ANOTHER package installs nothing and the later method call returns undef with no error -- perl calls the handler
